schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Locally advanced unresectable pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma after 4 to 8 months of active chemotherapy, with no radiographic progression and a qualifying CA19-9 response.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Chemotherapy received: mFOLFIRINOX, FOLFIRINOX, or NALIRIFOX versus gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel. If both were used, stratify by the longer regimen, or by the first regimen if the durations were equal.

schema.label: Randomize 1:1

arms.label: Arm 1, standard of care
arms.text: Continue chemotherapy, or 50.4 Gy or 54 Gy in 1.8 Gy fractions with fluoropyrimidine, or observation. Observation is suggested only after 6 months of chemotherapy.

arms.label: Arm 2, dose-escalated RT
arms.text: Default 10 Gy x 5 (BED10 100 Gy). Alternative 3 Gy x 25 (BED10 97.5 Gy). If 5 fractions are not feasible, contact the principal investigator before using 25 fractions.

schema.note: Tumor treating fields are allowed with induction chemotherapy before randomization.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: 3-year overall survival from randomization.

eligibility: Pathologically proven pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, locally advanced and unresectable by NCCN criteria and institutional tumor board review.

4 to 8 months of active chemotherapy with FOLFIRINOX, NALIRIFOX, or gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel. Breaks do not count. A regimen may be switched for toxicity or a CA19-9 that is not declining, not for RECIST progression.
Registration within 45 days of the last day of pre-study chemotherapy.

Restaging after month 4 and before entry shows no progression. If baseline CA19-9 was above 37, the later value is under 200 or has fallen by at least 70%. If baseline CA19-9 was 37 or lower, it must remain 37 or lower.
No overlapping prior radiotherapy. No active duodenal or gastric ulcer and no direct tumor invasion of bowel or stomach. Age 18 or older. ECOG 0-2.

pretreatment.note: The table marks this required and does not give a day count.

pretreatment.window: Any time before chemotherapy through 30 days after it starts
pretreatment.note: AST and ALT at most 3 times the upper limit of normal. If baseline CA19-9 is above 37, concurrent bilirubin is at most 1.5 times the upper limit.
Response rule is in the eligibility criteria.

pretreatment.window: Baseline before chemotherapy. Restaging after month 4, before entry.
pretreatment.note: CT chest/abdomen/pelvis, CT plus MRI, or PET/CT. Restaging must show at least stable disease.
Marked required, without a day window.

schema.label: Step 1 registration
schema.text: Register and confirm payment coverage for treatment.

schema.label: Step 2, stratify and randomize 1:1
schema.text: Child-Pugh A vs B7. Extrahepatic disease yes vs no. Macrovascular invasion VP1/VP2/VV1 vs VP3/VP4/VV2/IVC. Systemic therapy IO/IO vs IO plus a VEGF inhibitor.

schema.label: Treatment
schema.text: Protocol treatment starts within 21 days after randomization. If SBRT and immunotherapy start on different days, both start by day 35.

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: Liver SBRT plus IO-based systemic therapy.

schema.note: Physician's choice of atezolizumab plus bevacizumab, durvalumab plus one dose of tremelimumab, or nivolumab plus ipilimumab followed by nivolumab. For atezolizumab/bevacizumab, holding bevacizumab from 2 weeks before SBRT until 2 weeks after is recommended.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Overall survival, liver SBRT plus immunotherapy versus immunotherapy alone.

eligibility: HCC with macrovascular invasion: enhancing thrombus with arterial enhancement and washout. Extrahepatic disease is allowed.
At most 5 discrete intrahepatic foci. Sum of diameters under 20 cm. No direct extension into stomach, duodenum, small bowel, or large bowel.
No fibrolamellar, sarcomatoid, or biphenotypic HCC. Child-Pugh A or B7. ECOG 0-2. Age 18 or older.
Pathologic confirmation is strongly recommended. A radiographic AASLD diagnosis is allowed, except when there is a prior or concurrent malignancy, in which case pathology is required.

Prior resection, TACE, or ablation is allowed. No prior systemic therapy or radioembolization for HCC, and no prior liver transplant. No prior radiotherapy that would overlap enough to cause excessive cumulative toxicity.
Step 2 requires confirmation that payment coverage exists for both arms.

pretreatment.item: Diagnosis of HCC, history and physical, liver-disease history
pretreatment.note: The table marks these required and does not give a day count.

pretreatment.item: ECOG, Child-Pugh, albumin, bilirubin, INR, mALBI
ANC, platelets, hemoglobin, creatinine clearance, ALT, AST, AFP

pretreatment.note: VP1/VP2/VV1 versus VP3/VP4/VV2/IVC.

pretreatment.item: CT chest plus CT or MRI pelvis, or PET/CT of chest, abdomen, and pelvis

pretreatment.note: Persons of childbearing potential.
Marked required, without a day window.

schema.label: Disease
schema.text: Pathologically proven adenocarcinoma of the prostate, meeting the high-risk definition in eligibility.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Pelvic nodal radiotherapy yes vs no. ADT duration under 18 months vs over 18 months. Second-generation antiandrogen yes vs no. Intraprostatic microboost yes vs no.

schema.label: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: ADT of 6 to 36 months is required. Intended duration, type, and use of a second-generation antiandrogen are declared at registration.

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: Conventional or moderate hypofractionation in 20 to 45 fractions.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Metastasis-free survival on conventional imaging.

eligibility: High-risk prostate adenocarcinoma: at least one of cT3a-T3b (cT4 is not allowed), PSA above 20 ng/mL before ADT, Gleason 8-10, or a pelvic node of at least 1.0 cm in short axis on conventional imaging. PSA taken on a 5-alpha reductase inhibitor is doubled.
Prostate volume under 100 cc before ADT. No M1 disease on conventional imaging. A negative PSMA PET may substitute for that staging.
No prior prostate radiotherapy that would overlap, no prior prostatectomy, and no prior focal or ablative prostate therapy.
Prior ADT is allowed only if it started at most 185 days before registration. The pre-ADT PSA defines the risk group.
No contraindication to prostate MRI, which is required for radiotherapy planning on both arms. Age 18 or older. ECOG 0-2.

pretreatment.note: Includes height and weight.
This is the value used to define high-risk disease.
CT, MRI, or an approved PET. A pelvic MRI is not required for this row. PSMA PET/CT fulfills it.
Bone scan or PSMA, fluciclovine, or NaF PET/CT.
Marked in the prior-to-radiation column, without a day window.

schema.label: Disease
schema.text: cT2-cT3N0 muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma of the bladder.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Clinical stage T2 vs T3. Planned radiosensitizer: cisplatin, gemcitabine, or mitomycin-C/5-FU. Neoadjuvant therapy yes vs no.

schema.label: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: Protocol treatment starts within 28 days after randomization. Arm 2 must use plan-of-the-day or online adaptive radiotherapy.

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: 4 weeks of radiosensitizing chemotherapy plus hypofractionated radiotherapy, 55 Gy in 20 fractions.

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: 4 weeks of radiosensitizing chemotherapy plus SBRT, 32.5 Gy in 5 fractions.

schema.note: Radiosensitizing chemotherapy is limited to the 4-week window. Missed or held doses are not made up.

schema.label: Primary question
schema.text: Non-inferiority of ultra-hypofractionation versus hypofractionation for 3-year bladder-intact event-free survival. The margin is 10% (50% to 40%), corresponding to a hazard ratio below 1.32.

eligibility: Histologic cT2-T3N0M0 urothelial carcinoma. Mixed urothelial carcinoma is allowed. Small cell carcinoma is not.
One TURBT before randomization. Maximal resection is attempted. Complete or partial resection are both allowed. A repeat TURBT after the initial TURBT is not required.
The window from TURBT pathology to randomization is 180 days. It extends to 240 days only when the patient has completed at least 3 cycles of neoadjuvant chemotherapy.

Staging of chest, abdomen, and pelvis with CT or MRI, or FDG PET, before randomization. No T4, node-positive, or metastatic disease. A node of 1.0 cm or larger in short axis requires a biopsy showing no tumor.
No diffuse CIS on cystoscopy and biopsy. No prior pelvic radiation. No urothelial carcinoma outside the bladder within 24 months, except upper-tract Ta, T1, or CIS after complete nephroureterectomy.
Age 18 or older. Zubrod performance status 0-2.

pretreatment.note: Extended to at most 240 days before randomization only after at least 3 cycles of neoadjuvant chemotherapy. A repeat TURBT is not required.
CT of chest, abdomen, and pelvis, or CT of chest and abdomen plus MRI of the pelvis, or FDG PET-CT.
Persons of childbearing potential.
The pretreatment table does not give these a day window.

schema.label: Muscle-invasive disease
schema.text: Histologic cT2-T4aN0 urothelial carcinoma of the bladder.

schema.label: Neoadjuvant therapy
schema.text: Physician's choice, limited to the FDA-approved regimens in the eligibility criteria.

schema.label: Response assessment
schema.text: cT0 or cT1 on a repeat TURBT with systematic biopsies. That TURBT is within 90 days before registration.

schema.label: Registration
schema.text: Within 90 days after the last neoadjuvant dose.

schema.label: Treatment
schema.text: Bladder radiotherapy plus pembrolizumab for 1 year. Central radiation-plan approval is required before treatment starts. Radiotherapy is whole bladder only, 55 Gy in 20 fractions of 2.75 Gy, with no pelvic nodes and no tumor boost.

schema.label: On-study assessment
schema.text: Cystoscopy, cytology, and imaging.

schema.label: Endpoint
schema.text: 3-year bladder-intact event-free survival. Follow-up continues for 5 years after registration.

eligibility: Histologic cT2-T4aN0M0 muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma of the bladder within 180 days before neoadjuvant therapy starts. Staging CT, MRI, or PET of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis within 60 days before neoadjuvant therapy.

After neoadjuvant therapy, a repeat TURBT must show cT0 or cT1. It biopsies the prior disease and systematic sites (left and right lateral walls, dome, posterior wall, and trigone), with at least 4 of 5 systematic biopsies. The TURBT is within 60 days after the last neoadjuvant dose and within 90 days before registration.

No cT2 or higher, N1-3, or M1 disease after neoadjuvant therapy. A node of 1.0 cm or larger in short axis after neoadjuvant therapy needs PET-CT within 70 days before registration. A PET-positive node is ineligible unless biopsy shows no tumor.

At least 3 and no more than 6 cycles of FDA-approved neoadjuvant therapy: cisplatin-based combination chemotherapy, with or without a PD-1/L1 inhibitor; dose-dense or accelerated MVAC; or enfortumab vedotin with a PD-1/L1 inhibitor.
No small cell, neuroendocrine, or plasmacytoid histology. Mixed histology is allowed when more than half of the tumor is urothelial carcinoma. No prior pelvic radiotherapy.
The primary objective is written for clinically T0 or T1 disease without multifocal CIS. That CIS phrase is not an eligibility criterion.

pretreatment.window: Within 180 days before neoadjuvant therapy starts
pretreatment.note: Confirms muscle-invasive disease before systemic therapy.

pretreatment.item: Staging CT, MRI, or PET of chest, abdomen, and pelvis
pretreatment.note: Sets the pre-treatment stage.

pretreatment.window: Within 60 days after the last neoadjuvant dose, and within 90 days before registration
pretreatment.note: Must show cT0 or cT1. At least 4 of 5 systematic sites, plus the areas of prior disease.

pretreatment.item: Restaging chest, abdomen, and pelvis imaging
pretreatment.window: Within 60 days after the last neoadjuvant dose
pretreatment.note: CT or MRI, contrast preferred, or FDG PET-CT.

pretreatment.item: PET-CT for a node 1.0 cm or larger after neoadjuvant therapy
pretreatment.note: A PET-positive node requires a biopsy showing no tumor.

pretreatment.item: History and physical, CBC, chemistry, creatinine
pretreatment.note: The study calendar places these in the pre-registration column.

pretreatment.window: Within 90 days after the last neoadjuvant dose
pretreatment.note: Pembrolizumab is planned within 28 days after registration. Radiotherapy starts within 7 days of pembrolizumab and within 35 days after registration.
